transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because I’ve gotten to where I plan my whole summer around avoiding wasps. It's just getting to be too much. I've even given up my garden jobs at the church because of it. And at home, if I so much as hear buzzing, I end up making my husband unload things by the back porch. I just can't be around them at all.
When you hear buzzing or are near wasps, do you experience any physical reactions like sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, or difficulty breathing?

Yes, I do. The second I hear that sharp buzzing by the porch, or... or if I see one hovering near the flowers, my heart just jumps. My hands start to shake, and I just feel like I have to get inside right away.
How long have you felt this way about wasps, and has this fear affected any other parts of your life besides gardening and being outside at home?

Well, it's been going on since we had some remodeling done and uncovered a wasp nest... that was about two years and five months ago. Ever since that happened, I just haven't been able to deal with them at all. 

As for other parts of my life, it's mostly just what I mentioned—the gardening and trying to enjoy my own yard. But since I don't work and I'm at home most of the day, not being able to step outside without worrying about it really just gets in the way of everything I want to do.
Have you found yourself avoiding other places or activities where wasps might be, like picnics, parks, or outdoor events?

Well, yes. I mean, like I said about the church, I've had to completely step back from the gardening group there. But I've also stopped hosting garden days at my own house. That... well, that used to be a really big part of how I stayed connected with people, my friends and neighbors, so I really miss it. I just avoid those kinds of outdoor gatherings now. And even just day-to-day, my husband has basically had to take over all the porch and garden tasks that I used to handle myself. I just can't risk being out there.
Do you ever feel anxious or have panic symptoms, like a racing heart or shaking, even when you're just thinking about wasps or worried one might show up?

No, not really. I mean, I don't like thinking about them, of course, but just the thought of them doesn't make my heart race or anything like that. It's really only when I actually hear that buzzing or see one that the panic sets in. If I'm just sitting inside and thinking about them, I feel fine.
Do you notice that your anxiety or panic comes on very suddenly and peaks within a few minutes when you see a wasp or hear buzzing?

Yes, exactly. The second I hear that sharp buzzing out by the porch, or if I see one hovering near the flowers, it's just immediate. My heart jumps, my hands start to shake, and I just feel like I have to get inside right away. It doesn't build up slowly at all; it just hits me all at once the moment I realize one is there.
When you start feeling that panic when you see or hear a wasp, do you ever feel like you’re losing control, going crazy, or that you might die?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel like I'm going crazy or dying. It's just a really strong urge to get away, you know? I just feel very afraid and need to get back inside the house as fast as I can. But I don't feel like I'm losing my mind or anything like that.
Do you find yourself avoiding any other situations or places, even if they aren’t related to wasps, because you’re worried about feeling anxious or panicky?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to the grocery store, run my errands, and visit my friends. I don't avoid anything else. It's really just the wasps that bother me. If there aren't any wasps around, I'm perfectly fine going about my day.
Have you ever experienced sudden panic or anxiety in situations that don’t involve wasps, like being in crowded places, open spaces, or using public transportation?

No, I haven't. I'm completely fine in crowds or taking the bus or anything like that. I don't get panicky in open spaces either. It's really just the wasps. If there are no wasps around, I don't have any of those sudden feelings of panic at all.
Do you feel that your fear of wasps is excessive or unreasonable, and have you experienced this same level of fear with any other insects or animals?

Well, yes, I suppose I know it's a bit much. I mean, I know a wasp is just a little insect, and most folks would just swat it away or ignore it. But to me... it just feels like something terrible is about to happen if one gets anywhere near me. It's just this overwhelming feeling. And no, I don't get like this with anything else. Spiders, bees, dogs... none of that bothers me. It's just the wasps.
When you see or hear a wasp and start feeling that panic, do you always try to escape or avoid the situation immediately, and has this led to major changes in how you live your daily life?

Yes, I absolutely try to get away from them right away. If I see one, I just have to leave the area immediately. And... well, it has changed things for me, yes. I used to be very involved with the church gardening group, but I’ve had to step back from that entirely. I also stopped hosting garden days at my house, which is tough because that was a big part of how I stayed connected with people. Even just around my own house, my husband has had to take over all the porch and garden tasks that I used to handle myself, just so I don't have to be out there.
Do you ever have panic attacks that start even when you aren’t near wasps or thinking about them, or does the panic only happen when you actually see or hear a wasp?

No, it's really just when the wasps are around. I don't ever just... start panicking for no reason. If I'm inside and I know there aren't any wasps, I feel perfectly fine. The panic only ever happens if I actually see one or hear it buzzing near me.
Is your panic always triggered immediately by seeing or hearing a wasp, and do you ever feel anxious beforehand because you're worried one might appear?

Yes, it's pretty much instant. The second I hear that sharp buzzing out by the porch, or if I see one hovering near the flowers... my heart just jumps. My hands start to shake, and I just feel this overwhelming urge that I have to get inside right away. And as for worrying beforehand... yes, I do. If I know I have to go outside, especially in the summer when they're active, I start getting anxious before I even open the door, just anticipating that one might be out there.

Has your fear of wasps led to any additional avoidance behaviors beyond what we’ve already discussed, such as avoiding certain rooms in your house or making major changes to your routine during certain times of the year?

Well, like I mentioned, I really plan my whole summer around avoiding them. Giving up the church gardening was a big one, but it also affects how I do things at home. If I hear buzzing near the back porch, I just won't go out there at all. I'll actually make my husband unload the groceries or bring things in if I think there might be wasps around. I just can't be out there if there's even a chance they're near the doors.
If you see a wasp that is far away or in a place where it can't reach you, like inside a closed container or behind a window, do you still feel the need to escape or become very anxious?

If it's behind a window or something like that, I still get pretty anxious, honestly. Even if I know it can't get to me right that second, I just can't relax until it's gone. I know a wasp is just a little insect and most folks would just swat it away or ignore it, but to me... it just feels like something terrible is about to happen if one gets anywhere near me. So even seeing one safely behind glass, my heart still races and I just want to get away from it.
Do you feel that your fear of wasps is out of proportion to the actual danger they pose, even though you know they are just small insects?

Yes, I do. Like I said before, I know it's just a little bug. Most people wouldn't think twice about it, they'd just swat it away or ignore it. But for me, it's... it's just different. I know it doesn't make sense, but it just feels like something awful is going to happen if one gets close to me. It's definitely out of proportion, but I just can't help how I react.
Has your fear of wasps remained consistent since the nest was uncovered, and has it caused you significant distress or affected your life in ways beyond just avoiding wasps?

Yes, it's been pretty consistent. This whole thing started when we were doing that remodel and uncovered the big wasp nest... that was about two years and five months ago. Since then, it's just been a constant issue. It definitely causes me a lot of distress, especially in the summer, and like I mentioned with the gardening and making my husband do things outside, it really has changed how I live day-to-day.
